original.target_description: Anderson et al. (2012), Study 5: need for dominance predicting the combined residual-based overconfidence index in simultaneous regression with need for affiliation, need for achievement, and all Big Five dimensions; US MTurk sample. Target located in Table 3 of author manuscript rather than supplied p.79.

n.sample_role: Participants; Study 5 recruitment sample is 77 US MTurk respondents, but the analytic N for the eight-predictor regression is not explicitly printed.
n.exclusions: No exclusions or missing-data handling for the target regression are documented in the located Study 5 text.
n.location: Author manuscript p.36 (PDF p.38), Participants; Table 3 (PDF p.72) has no N.
n.quote: Our sample included 77 individuals from around the United States (60% male). The data were collected online, using MTurk.

es.location: Table 3, Study 5: Need for Dominance Predicts Overconfidence; PDF p.72; corroborated manuscript p.39 (PDF p.41).

p.location: Table 3, Need for Dominance row and asterisk footnote; PDF p.72.

replication.target_description: Mayiwar et al. (2025), Study 1 direct replication using the original PRF need-for-dominance measure: standardized multiple regression predicting the average residual-based overconfidence index from three needs and Big Five traits. Full-sample direct replication model, not alternative-measure or exclusion robustness analyses.

n.sample_role: Observations (US Prolific participants) in the direct replication regression.
n.exclusions: Primary analysis uses full sample. Seventeen Study 1 participants were excluded only in a separate robustness analysis, not the target Table 5 model.
n.location: p.29, Table 5, Observations row, Replication model (same needs measures); pp.27–28 exclusion discussion.

es.location: p.29, Table 5, Need for Dominance (Status) row, Replication model (same needs measures), β column.

p.location: p.29, Table 5, Need for Dominance (Status) row, Replication model (same needs measures), p column.

reported_success.location: p.31, conclusion of Direct Replication Test (Using the Same Needs Measures).
reported_success.quote: Overall, we conclude this to be a successful replication of the target article, yet with a much weaker effect for the status-overconfidence relationship than the original effect.

notes: Original primary author manuscript acquired from Vanderbilt author publication PDF; title and authors match reference. DOI landing page inaccessible; first author-hosted PDF route returned 403, then Vanderbilt alternative succeeded. Supplied original locator p.79 is not a page of this manuscript; Study 5 and exact target regression were matched independently. Original analytic n remains null: 77 is printed as the Study 5 sample, but not explicitly as regression analytic N. No original statistics were substituted from the replication paper. Original Table 3 explicitly prints p = .010 via the dominance-row asterisk, despite the replication paper stating original p-values were not reported. Replication t = 3.78, p = .957 is an equivalence test and was not paired with the target regression beta. Frozen replication cache used without modification.
